items.title: Warren "Baby" Dodds Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: Well, there were Henri Dutre, trombone, with my brother John Clannett and Eddie Garland on bass file.

ctx.x: Okay, it's going. Baby, since Joe Oliver isn't around anymore, I thought I'd ask you a few questions about Oliver and his band. At the time you knew him, that you played with him, how did you enjoy working with the band? Well, Bill, as far as the band's concerned, it was a swell band to work with. Everybody knew what they were doing, everybody was set with anything went off, everybody was ready. When did you join the Oliver band? Well, I joined the Oliver band by the year of 1921. I left the Stuckford's line in…

Okay, I guess it's going again. We might talk a little bit about Dutre too since he isn't here anymore to talk for himself. No, he was a comical guy. That was a comical man. Really comical. He was really comical. A man could bring a tail to tell you before you get off work, you got a tail to tell you when you get off work. After you get off work, you got one to tell you to keep your company all the way. If you stay out five hours, you got a tail to tell you for five hours. He was a great character. I was for the…

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: Baby Dots was playing in St. Louis. He wrote to Baby Dots.

ctx.x: So, you know, alright. Baby Dots was playing in St. Louis. He wrote to Baby Dots. And he said for Baby Dots. Now, he didn't get permission from the union. Number six, you see. Baby Dots. Baby Dots. After he sent for Baby Dots, we went down to the union and reported it. Ram did. Oh, he called in Joe. He called Joe in. He went to the trial board. He had me there and Ram there. Cause he asked me questions. I told him, yeah. Told him how it just happened. They found out that Baby Dots was unfinancial. In the union,…

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: All right, Baby was all right.

ctx.x: How was Baby -- How as Baby Dotson to play with?
All right, Baby was all right.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: He sent for Baby Dolls in St. Louis.

ctx.x: Yeah. That was great. He sent for Baby Dolls in St. Louis. He don't consult with the board. You see, when you get ready to send somebody, you got to go consult with the board. At the union? The union. Get the permission to send for a man. He don't know if the man's in good standing or not. He sent for him. The boy come and he was in bad standing in St. Louis. The boy comes, a man goes on down to number six. I go with him, I don't know what happened. Then they had us all to come on up to number six. And they found…
tell us a little about those first records that you made with Ori. Now, how did that come about?
